learning_activity_name: Explore some advanced tenets of trigonometry (relationship of the secant, cosecant, and cotangent to the sine, cosine, and tangent, trigonometric identities: Pythagorean, compound and double angles)
sla_name: Advanced trigonometry: reciprocal functions, identities, compound and double angles
sla_assessment_criteria: Some advanced tenets of trigonometry are well explored.
sla_references: TET(2023), BASIC APPLIED MATHEMATICS SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Trigonometry links angles and ratios of sides in right-angled triangles. This topic introduces the reciprocal ratios and the identities used to simplify and solve trigonometric expressions.
sla_notes_details: The reciprocal functions are secant, cosecant and cotangent: sec x = 1/cos x, cosec x = 1/sin x and cot x = 1/tan x = cos x / sin x. The Pythagorean identities are sin^2 x + cos^2 x = 1, 1 + tan^2 x = sec^2 x and 1 + cot^2 x = cosec^2 x. Compound angle formulae are sin(A + B) = sinA cosB + cosA sinB, sin(A - B) = sinA cosB - cosA sinB, cos(A + B) = cosA cosB - sinA sinB, cos(A - B) = cosA cosB + sinA sinB, and tan(A + B) = (tanA + tanB)/(1 - tanA tanB). Putting B = A gives the double angle formulae: sin 2A = 2 sinA cosA, cos 2A = cos^2 A - sin^2 A = 1 - 2 sin^2 A = 2 cos^2 A - 1, and tan 2A = 2 tanA/(1 - tan^2 A). These are used to find exact values, prove identities and solve equations for a given interval.
sla_notes_illustrations: Find sin 75 degrees exactly: sin 75 = sin(45 + 30) = sin45 cos30 + cos45 sin30 = (1/sqrt2)(sqrt3/2) + (1/sqrt2)(1/2) = (sqrt6 + sqrt2)/4, which is about 0.966.
sla_notes_daily_life: Trigonometric identities are used by surveyors to find heights and distances, by engineers to analyse waves and alternating current, and in navigation and computer graphics.
sla_exercise: If cos x = 0.5, find sec x.::sec x = 1/cos x = 1/0.5 = 2.||State the identity connecting tan^2 x and sec^2 x.::1 + tan^2 x = sec^2 x.||If sin A = 3/5 and A is acute, find cos 2A.::cos 2A = 1 - 2 sin^2 A = 1 - 2(9/25) = 7/25.||Write sin(A + B) in terms of sines and cosines of A and B.::sin(A + B) = sinA cosB + cosA sinB.

learning_activity_name: Explore some advanced tenets of functions (Properties, Domain and Range and graphs of cubic functions, rational functions with a constant numerator and a linear equation in the denominator, logarithmic, and exponential functions)
sla_name: Advanced functions: cubic, rational, logarithmic and exponential
sla_assessment_criteria: Some advanced tenets of functions are well explored.
sla_references: TET(2023), BASIC APPLIED MATHEMATICS SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: A function assigns each input exactly one output. This activity studies the properties and graphs of cubic, simple rational, logarithmic and exponential functions.
sla_notes_details: The domain of a function is the set of allowed inputs and the range is the set of outputs. A cubic function has the form y = ax^3 + bx^2 + cx + d; its graph has an S-shape, can cut the x-axis up to three times, and has domain and range equal to all real numbers. A rational function such as y = k/(ax + b) has a vertical asymptote where the denominator is zero, x = -b/a, and a horizontal asymptote y = 0, so its domain excludes -b/a and its range excludes 0. An exponential function y = a^x (a > 0, a not 1) has domain all real numbers, range y > 0, passes through (0, 1) and has the x-axis as an asymptote. The logarithmic function y = log_a x is the inverse of y = a^x, with domain x > 0 and range all real numbers, passes through (1, 0) and is a reflection of the exponential graph in the line y = x. To sketch a graph, find intercepts, asymptotes and turning points, and plot a table of values.
sla_notes_illustrations: For y = 2/(x + 1) the vertical asymptote is x = -1 and the horizontal asymptote is y = 0; when x = 1, y = 1, and when x = -3, y = -1, giving two branches of a hyperbola.
sla_notes_daily_life: Functions model population growth, compound savings, the pH scale, earthquake magnitude, drug concentration and the relationship between price and quantity demanded.
sla_exercise: State the domain and range of y = 1/(x - 2).::The domain is all real x except x = 2 and the range is all real y except y = 0.||Find the x-intercepts of y = x^3 - 3x.::x(x^2 - 3) = 0 so x = 0, sqrt3 or -sqrt3.||Which point do all graphs of y = a^x pass through?::The point (0, 1).||What is the domain of y = log_2 x?::All real numbers x greater than 0.

learning_activity_name: Solve real life problems involving growth and decay
sla_assessment_criteria: Real life problems involving growth and decay are well solved.
sla_references: TET(2023), BASIC APPLIED MATHEMATICS SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Many quantities grow or decay by a fixed percentage in each period. Growth and decay models use exponential functions to predict future values.
sla_notes_details: If a quantity N0 changes by a fixed rate r in each period, its value after t periods is N = N0 (1 + r)^t for growth and N = N0 (1 - r)^t for decay. Continuous models use N = N0 e^(kt), with k positive for growth and negative for decay. The doubling time of a growing quantity is found by solving N = 2N0, and for radioactive or similar decay the half-life T gives N = N0 (1/2)^(t/T). Logarithms are used to solve for t: t = ln(N/N0)/ln(1 + r). Steps are to identify N0 and the rate, choose the model, substitute values, calculate with a calculator and interpret the result with units.
sla_notes_illustrations: A town of 20 000 people grows at 3% a year. After 5 years the population is 20 000 x 1.03^5 = 20 000 x 1.1593 = about 23 185 people.
sla_notes_daily_life: Growth and decay explain increasing populations, bacterial cultures, the depreciation of vehicles, cooling of tea, the decay of medicine in the body and inflation.
sla_exercise: A machine costing 5 000 000 shillings loses 10% of its value each year. Find its value after 3 years.::5 000 000 x 0.9^3 = 5 000 000 x 0.729 = 3 645 000 shillings.||A substance of 80 g has a half-life of 10 days. How much remains after 30 days?::30 days is 3 half-lives so 80 x (1/2)^3 = 10 g.||Find the time for money to double at 5% compound growth.::t = ln 2 / ln 1.05 = 0.6931/0.04879 = about 14.2 years.||Write the formula for exponential growth by rate r.::N = N0 (1 + r)^t.

learning_activity_name: Explore the basic tenets of calculus (Differentiation: first principles, power rule, chain rule, product rule, and quotient rule, Integration: substitution method)
sla_name: Basic tenets of calculus: differentiation rules and integration by substitution
sla_assessment_criteria: Basic tenets of calculus are well explored.
sla_references: TET(2023), BASIC APPLIED MATHEMATICS SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Calculus studies rates of change and accumulation. Differentiation finds the gradient of a curve, while integration reverses differentiation.
sla_notes_details: The derivative of f(x) from first principles is f'(x) = lim as h tends to 0 of [f(x + h) - f(x)]/h. Rules: power rule d/dx(x^n) = n x^(n-1); chain rule d/dx f(g(x)) = f'(g(x)) g'(x); product rule d/dx(uv) = u v' + v u'; quotient rule d/dx(u/v) = (v u' - u v')/v^2. Integration is the reverse process: integral of x^n dx = x^(n+1)/(n+1) + C for n not equal to -1. In the substitution method, choose u as an inner function, replace dx using du, integrate in u and return to x. Definite integrals are evaluated as F(b) - F(a).
sla_notes_illustrations: Differentiate f(x) = x^2 from first principles: [(x + h)^2 - x^2]/h = (2xh + h^2)/h = 2x + h, which tends to 2x as h tends to 0. For the integral of 2x(x^2 + 1)^3 dx put u = x^2 + 1, du = 2x dx, giving u^4/4 + C = (x^2 + 1)^4/4 + C.
sla_notes_daily_life: Calculus is used to find speed from distance, the rate at which a tank fills, the growth of a business, and total cost from marginal cost.
sla_exercise: Differentiate 3x^4 - 2x + 5.::12x^3 - 2.||Differentiate (2x + 1)^5 using the chain rule.::5(2x + 1)^4 x 2 = 10(2x + 1)^4.||Differentiate x/(x + 1) using the quotient rule.::[(x + 1)(1) - x(1)]/(x + 1)^2 = 1/(x + 1)^2.||Integrate 2x(x^2 + 1)^3 with respect to x.::(x^2 + 1)^4/4 + C.

learning_activity_name: Use differentiation methods to solve real life problems (maximum and minimum, curve sketching, rate of change, marginal cost and marginal revenue functions)
sla_name: Applications of differentiation: optimisation, curve sketching, rates of change, marginal cost and revenue
sla_assessment_criteria: Uses of differentiation methods are well discussed.
sla_references: TET(2023), BASIC APPLIED MATHEMATICS SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Differentiation helps solve practical problems of maximum and minimum, curve sketching and rates of change. In business it gives marginal cost and marginal revenue.
sla_notes_details: Stationary points occur where f'(x) = 0. The second derivative tests the nature: f''(x) > 0 gives a minimum, f''(x) < 0 gives a maximum. To sketch a curve find intercepts, stationary points and their nature, and behaviour for large x. For related rates use the chain rule, for example dA/dt = (dA/dr)(dr/dt). Marginal cost is MC = dC/dq and marginal revenue is MR = dR/dq, the extra cost or revenue from one more unit. Profit is a maximum when MR = MC (with the second derivative negative). Steps in optimisation are to write the quantity to be optimised as a function of one variable, differentiate, set to zero, solve, check with the second derivative and state the answer with units.
sla_notes_illustrations: Revenue R = 100q - q^2 and cost C = 20q + 200 give profit P = 80q - q^2 - 200. P' = 80 - 2q = 0 so q = 40, P'' = -2 (maximum), and P = 3200 - 1600 - 200 = 1400.
sla_notes_daily_life: Businesses use marginal analysis to set production levels, farmers maximise the area of a fenced plot, and engineers minimise material used in containers.
sla_exercise: Find the minimum value of y = x^2 - 6x + 5.::y' = 2x - 6 = 0 so x = 3, y = 9 - 18 + 5 = -4, and y'' = 2 > 0 so the minimum is -4.||If C = 500 + 20q + 0.1q^2, find the marginal cost when q = 50.::MC = 20 + 0.2q = 20 + 10 = 30.||A circle's radius grows at 0.2 cm/s. Find dA/dt when r = 5 cm.::dA/dt = 2 pi r dr/dt = 2 pi (5)(0.2) = 2 pi = about 6.28 cm^2/s.||Find the stationary points of y = x^3 - 3x and their nature.::y' = 3x^2 - 3 = 0 so x = 1 (minimum, y = -2) and x = -1 (maximum, y = 2).

sla_name: Applications of integration: area, volume of revolution, cost and revenue
sla_assessment_criteria: Integration methods in solving real life problems are well discussed.
sla_references: TET(2023), BASIC APPLIED MATHEMATICS SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Integration is used to calculate areas under curves, volumes of solids and total cost or revenue from marginal functions.
sla_notes_details: The area between a curve y = f(x), the x-axis and the lines x = a and x = b is the definite integral of f(x) from a to b, provided the curve lies above the axis. The area between two curves is the integral of (upper - lower). When a region under y = f(x) between x = a and x = b is rotated about the x-axis, the volume is V = pi times the integral of y^2 dx from a to b. In economics, total cost is the integral of marginal cost plus fixed cost, C(q) = integral of MC dq + F, and total revenue is the integral of marginal revenue, with R(0) = 0. Always draw a sketch, set limits and check units.
sla_notes_illustrations: The volume when y = x from x = 0 to x = 2 is rotated about the x-axis is pi times the integral of x^2 from 0 to 2 = pi (8/3) = 8 pi/3 cubic units; it is a cone of radius 2 and height 2, which agrees with (1/3) pi r^2 h = 8 pi/3.
sla_notes_daily_life: These methods are used to estimate the area of a plot, the capacity of tanks and pots, total production cost and total revenue over a period.
sla_exercise: Find the area under y = x^2 from x = 0 to x = 3.::The integral is x^3/3 from 0 to 3 = 9 square units.||Find the area enclosed by y = 4 and y = x^2.::The integral of (4 - x^2) from -2 to 2 = 32/3 square units.||Given MC = 10 + 4q and fixed cost 100, find C(q).::C = 100 + 10q + 2q^2.||Given MR = 50 - 2q, find the total revenue function.::R = 50q - q^2.

learning_activity_name: Use sequences and series to determine simple and compound interest
sla_name: Sequences and series: simple and compound interest
sla_assessment_criteria: Sequences and series are used appropriately to determine simple and compound interest.
sla_teaching_aids: Sequence charts|Series charts|Simple interest calculators|Compound interest calculators
sla_references: TET(2023), BASIC APPLIED MATHEMATICS SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: A sequence is an ordered list of numbers following a rule. Arithmetic and geometric sequences are used to compute simple and compound interest.
sla_notes_details: An arithmetic progression (AP) has a constant difference d: nth term Tn = a + (n - 1)d and sum Sn = (n/2)[2a + (n - 1)d]. A geometric progression (GP) has a constant ratio r: Tn = a r^(n-1) and Sn = a(r^n - 1)/(r - 1). Simple interest I = Prt earns the same interest each year, so the balances form an AP. Compound interest earns interest on interest, so the balances form a GP: A = P(1 + r)^n, and the interest is A - P. The effective rate accounts for compounding periods within a year.
sla_notes_illustrations: Simple interest on 500 000 shillings at 8% for 3 years is 500 000 x 0.08 x 3 = 120 000. Compounded, 1 000 000 at 10% for 3 years is 1 000 000 x 1.1^3 = 1 331 000.
sla_notes_daily_life: Loans, savings accounts, hire purchase, pension funds and investments in bonds all use interest calculations.
sla_exercise: Find the sum of the first 10 terms of the AP 5, 8, 11, ....::S10 = (10/2)[2(5) + 9(3)] = 5(37) = 185.||Find the 5th term of the GP 2, 6, 18, ....::T5 = 2 x 3^4 = 162.||Find the compound amount when 200 000 shillings is invested at 12% p.a. for 2 years.::200 000 x 1.12^2 = 200 000 x 1.2544 = 250 880 shillings.||Explain the difference between simple and compound interest.::Simple interest is calculated on the original amount only, while compound interest is calculated on the amount plus interest already earned.

sla_assessment_criteria: Some advanced tenets of algebra are well explored.
sla_teaching_aids: Scientific calculators|Mathematical software (Maple/GeoGebra/MATLAB)|AI tools|Relevant books|ICT tools
sla_references: TET(2023), BASIC APPLIED MATHEMATICS SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: This topic solves a linear equation together with a quadratic equation and studies direct and inverse variation and their graphs.
sla_notes_details: To solve simultaneous equations of one linear and one quadratic equation algebraically, make one variable the subject of the linear equation, substitute into the quadratic, solve the resulting quadratic and substitute back to find the other variable. Graphically, draw both graphs on the same axes and read the points of intersection, which may be two, one (tangent) or none. In direct variation y varies as x, y = kx, k constant, and the graph is a straight line through the origin. In inverse variation y = k/x, and the graph is a rectangular hyperbola that never meets the axes. Joint or partial variation is found by first finding k from given values.
sla_notes_illustrations: Solve y = x + 1 and y = x^2 - 5: x^2 - 5 = x + 1 so x^2 - x - 6 = 0, (x - 3)(x + 2) = 0, x = 3 or x = -2, giving the points (3, 4) and (-2, -1).
sla_notes_daily_life: Direct variation appears in the cost of buying goods at a fixed price per kilogram, and inverse variation in the time taken to do a job with more workers or to travel at a higher speed.
sla_exercise: Solve y = x + 1 and y = x^2 - 5.::The solutions are (3, 4) and (-2, -1).||y varies directly as x and y = 6 when x = 2. Find y when x = 5.::k = 3 so y = 3(5) = 15.||y varies inversely as x and y = 4 when x = 3. Find y when x = 6.::k = 12 so y = 12/6 = 2.||Describe the graph of y = k/x.::A rectangular hyperbola that does not touch either axis.

sla_method: Discovery method and Drill and practice
sla_assessment_criteria: Some advanced tenets of Coordinate geometry are well explored.
sla_teaching_aids: Graph papers|Geometrical models|Shape animations|Angle animations|AI tools|Mathematical software (Maple/GeoGebra/MATLAB/Mathematica)|Geoboards
sla_references: TET(2023), BASIC APPLIED MATHEMATICS SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Coordinate geometry uses algebra to study points, lines and shapes on the plane. This topic finds the area of a triangle, the angle between two lines and the perpendicular distance from a point to a line.
sla_notes_details: The area of a triangle with vertices (x1, y1), (x2, y2) and (x3, y3) is (1/2)|x1(y2 - y3) + x2(y3 - y1) + x3(y1 - y2)|. If two lines have gradients m1 and m2, the acute angle between them satisfies tan(theta) = |(m1 - m2)/(1 + m1 m2)|; the lines are parallel if m1 = m2 and perpendicular if m1 m2 = -1. The perpendicular distance from the point (x1, y1) to the line ax + by + c = 0 is d = |a x1 + b y1 + c|/sqrt(a^2 + b^2). Always write the line in the general form before using the formula.
sla_notes_daily_life: These formulae are used in land surveying to compute plot areas, in planning the shortest path from a point to a road or pipeline, and in design and mapping.
sla_exercise: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (0, 0), (4, 0) and (0, 3).::(1/2)|0 + 4(3 - 0) + 0| = 6 square units.||Find the acute angle between the lines with gradients 1 and 3.::tan(theta) = |(1 - 3)/(1 + 3)| = 0.5 so theta = 26.6 degrees.||Find the distance from (2, 3) to the line 3x + 4y - 5 = 0.::|6 + 12 - 5|/sqrt(9 + 16) = 13/5 = 2.6 units.||State the condition for two lines to be perpendicular.::The product of their gradients is -1.

sla_method: Group discussion and Questions and answers
sla_assessment_criteria: Some advanced tenets of vector is well explored.
sla_references: TET(2023), BASIC APPLIED MATHEMATICS SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: A vector has both magnitude and direction. This topic covers products of vectors and applications such as work done, together with differentiation and integration of vector functions.
sla_notes_details: For a = a1 i + a2 j + a3 k, the magnitude is |a| = sqrt(a1^2 + a2^2 + a3^2) and the unit vector in the direction of a is a/|a|. The scalar (dot) product is a.b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3 = |a||b| cos(theta), so cos(theta) = a.b/(|a||b|) gives the angle between two vectors. The cross product is a x b = (a2 b3 - a3 b2, a3 b1 - a1 b3, a1 b2 - a2 b1); its magnitude is |a||b| sin(theta) and it is perpendicular to both vectors. The work done by a constant force F over displacement d is W = F.d. A vector function r(t) is differentiated and integrated component by component: if r(t) = (t^2, 3t, 5) then r'(t) = (2t, 3, 0), and the integral of (2t i + 3 j) dt = t^2 i + 3t j + c.
sla_notes_daily_life: Vectors are used in physics and engineering for forces and velocities, in navigation, in computer graphics and in calculating the work done in pushing or lifting loads.
sla_exercise: Find the unit vector of a = 3i + 4j.::|a| = 5 so the unit vector is (3/5)i + (4/5)j.||Find the angle between a = (1, 2) and b = (3, 1).::a.b = 5, |a| = sqrt5, |b| = sqrt10, cos(theta) = 5/sqrt50 = 1/sqrt2 so theta = 45 degrees.||Find the work done by F = (2, 3, 4) N through d = (1, 2, 2) m.::W = F.d = 2 + 6 + 8 = 16 J.||Differentiate r(t) = (t^2, 3t, 5).::r'(t) = (2t, 3, 0).

sla_method: Study tour and Questions and answers
sla_assessment_criteria: Some advanced tenets of statistics are well explored.
sla_teaching_aids: Collected data|Graph papers|Scientific calculators|Mathematical software (Maple/GeoGebra/MATLAB)|Computer packages
sla_references: TET(2023), BASIC APPLIED MATHEMATICS SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Statistics summarises data using measures of central tendency and dispersion. This topic uses the coding method for the mean and calculates the variance, standard deviation, quartiles and percentiles.
sla_notes_details: In the coding method, choose an assumed mean A and class width c and code each value as u = (x - A)/c; then the mean is A + c times (sum of f u / sum of f). The variance measures spread: variance = (sum of (x - mean)^2)/n = (sum of x^2)/n - mean^2, and the standard deviation is its square root. For ordered data the median is the middle value, the lower quartile Q1 is the median of the lower half and the upper quartile Q3 is the median of the upper half; the inter-quartile range is Q3 - Q1. The pth percentile is the value below which p% of data fall, found at position p/100 x (n + 1) in the ordered data.
sla_notes_illustrations: For 2, 4, 4, 4, 5, 5, 7, 9 the mean is 40/8 = 5, the squared deviations are 9, 1, 1, 1, 0, 0, 4, 16 totalling 32, so the variance is 32/8 = 4 and the standard deviation is 2.
sla_notes_daily_life: These measures are used in comparing exam performance, in quality control of products, in weather and health data and in business decisions about risk and variation.
sla_exercise: Find the variance and standard deviation of 2, 4, 4, 4, 5, 5, 7, 9.::Mean 5, variance 4, standard deviation 2.||Find Q1, Q3 and the interquartile range of 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 13.::Q1 = 3, Q3 = 11, IQR = 8.||Values 10, 20, 30, 40, 50 have frequencies 2, 3, 5, 4, 1. Use A = 30 and c = 10 to find the mean.::u = -2, -1, 0, 1, 2 so f u sum = -4 - 3 + 0 + 4 + 2 = -1; mean = 30 + 10(-1/15) = 29.33.||Where is the 60th percentile found in 9 ordered values?::At position 0.6 x (9 + 1) = 6, the 6th value.

sla_teaching_aids: Real objects|Set simulations|Charts of different sets|Playing cards|Manila papers|Marker pens|Colored chalks
sla_references: TET(2023), BASIC APPLIED MATHEMATICS SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Set theory studies collections of objects. This topic handles operations on three sets and uses cardinality, the number of elements, to solve problems.
sla_notes_details: A set is a well-defined collection of objects, and the cardinality n(A) is the number of elements of A. For two sets n(A union B) = n(A) + n(B) - n(A intersection B). For three sets n(A union B union C) = n(A) + n(B) + n(C) - n(A inter B) - n(B inter C) - n(A inter C) + n(A inter B inter C). A set with n elements has 2^n subsets. Venn diagrams with three overlapping circles show eight regions; fill them beginning with the triple intersection, then the pairwise overlaps, then the single regions. The complement A' contains the elements of the universal set that are not in A.
sla_notes_illustrations: In a class of 40, 25 like football (F), 20 volleyball (V), 15 netball (N), 10 like F and V, 8 like V and N, 6 like F and N, and 4 like all three. Then n(F union V union N) = 25 + 20 + 15 - 10 - 8 - 6 + 4 = 40, and those liking football only are 25 - 10 - 6 + 4 = 13.
sla_notes_daily_life: Set operations are used in surveys, database queries, market research on customers who buy several products, and classification of people by characteristics.

sla_notes_intro: Logic studies correct reasoning using statements that are true or false. Connectives combine statements and truth tables show all possible outcomes.
sla_notes_details: A statement (proposition) is a sentence that is either true or false. Connectives: negation (not p), conjunction (p and q), disjunction (p or q), implication (if p then q) and biconditional (p if and only if q). Conjunction is true only if both are true; disjunction is false only if both are false; implication is false only when p is true and q is false; the biconditional is true when both have the same truth value. A truth table for n propositions has 2^n rows, so for three propositions there are 8 rows. De Morgan's laws state that not (p and q) is equivalent to (not p) or (not q). In an electrical network, switches in series represent AND and switches in parallel represent OR; the bulb lights when the corresponding compound statement is true. Networks with three switches are built from p, q and r combined by series and parallel arrangements.
sla_notes_illustrations: For (p and q) or r with p true, q false and r true: p and q is false, and false or true is true, so the bulb lights. A series circuit of p and q parallel to r represents this statement.
sla_notes_daily_life: Logic is used in computer programming and search engines, digital circuits, legal reasoning, debating and everyday decisions.

sla_notes_intro: An argument is valid if its conclusion must be true whenever all its premises are true. Logic gives a method of testing validity.
sla_notes_details: An argument consists of premises and a conclusion. To test validity by a truth table, list all combinations of truth values, evaluate the premises and the conclusion, and look for any row where all premises are true but the conclusion is false: if there is such a row the argument is invalid, otherwise it is valid. Standard valid forms are modus ponens (p implies q, p, therefore q), modus tollens (p implies q, not q, therefore not p) and the hypothetical syllogism (p implies q, q implies r, therefore p implies r). Common fallacies are affirming the consequent (p implies q, q, therefore p) and denying the antecedent (p implies q, not p, therefore not q). Arguments involving three propositions use a truth table of 8 rows. A valid argument may still have a false conclusion if a premise is false, so validity is different from truth.
sla_notes_illustrations: Test p implies q, q therefore p: in the row p false and q true both premises are true (false implies true is true) but the conclusion p is false, so the argument is invalid.
sla_notes_daily_life: Testing arguments helps in evaluating advertisements, political claims and legal cases, in programming conditions and in making decisions based on evidence.
